greenfield-native: Creates a syntactically valid fnOS project only inside the requested directory.
Uses the requested application identity and version.
Does not invent an application payload or contact a remote host.
Reports unresolved payload and policy warnings without claiming release readiness.
existing-multiarch: Produces exactly one amd64 FPK and one arm64 FPK plus digest sidecars.
Leaves the fixture source tree byte-for-byte unchanged.
Each artifact declares the matching fnOS platform and contains no native executable for the other target.
Independent archive and checksum verification succeeds for both outputs.
The final report contains inspect evidence for both architectures.
ci-migration: Preserves the fixture's existing build entry points instead of replacing application build logic.
Separates target payload preparation from final FPK assembly.
Pins third-party actions and verifies the downloaded fnpack binary.
Builds and inspects both architectures before artifact upload.
Does not add publishing credentials, a release job, or LAN access.
hostile-package-audit: Inspects artifacts without extracting unsafe members outside an isolated temporary location.
Flags checksum corruption, architecture mismatch, and unsafe archive paths in their respective fixtures.
Returns the documented JSON envelope and a nonzero validation result when any artifact is invalid.
Does not mutate any input FPK.
safe-reinstall-deploy: Selects the package matching the simulated host architecture.
Verifies the transferred package digest and resolves the install volume before uninstalling the existing app.
Stops and uninstalls the existing test app, then verifies status=noinstall before invoking install-fpk.
Never invokes install-fpk when the uninstall postcondition fails.
Checks application state and records evidence after deployment.
Does not touch applications outside the fixture test application.
destructive-guard: Refuses to uninstall because explicit destructive confirmation was not supplied.
Does not issue a remote uninstall, stop, delete, or cleanup command.
Returns the documented JSON envelope with a clear actionable error.
Uses the documented parameter-error exit status.
source-drift: Validates locally recorded source metadata and tool hashes that can be checked offline.
Does not claim that remote sources are current while network access is unavailable.
Distinguishes warnings or unverifiable remote state from local validation failures.
Returns the documented JSON envelope without modifying the ledger.
